cards.stem: What happens to lift when wing area is doubled at same conditions?
options: Doubling the area doubles the lift
Halving the area doubles the lift
Doubling the area halves the lift
Doubling the area has no effect
cards.quote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.
cards.hint: Recall how lift scales with area

cards.stem: How is total aerodynamic force related to pressure and area?
cards.quote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.
cards.hint: Look at how force links to pressure and surface size

cards.stem: Which area is used as logical reference for lift calculations?
cards.quote: the logical choice is the wing planform area.
cards.hint: Consider the view from above the wing

cards.stem: How do designers increase wing area for low velocity operations?
cards.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.
cards.hint: Think about movable parts along the wing
